scientific_question: Do source-public previous selected action-specific consequences predict the *actually returned next public change* better than an information-matched falsified action-label history, and how much support exists? Offline retrospective predictive association only, not causal efficacy.

method.context: exact original mission+direction+public frontal pixel triple [3][5]
method.outcome: source public full original image+direction+mission SHA changed compared with authentic selected before
method.legality: original 7 selected actions, no offpolicy outcomes generated
method.negative_control_action_permutation: for a prior actual selected action a, assign its prior outcome label to (a+1) modulo 7, preserving original order, contexts, outcome counts and total history size; current action remains unpermuted
method.negative_control_outcome_inversion: invert only prior changed/not-changed outcomes with same context and original action, so exact support unchanged
method.matched_support: evaluate primary-vs-permuted Brier on current events where both histories contain prior context-selected action support, and primary-vs-inversion on all original-supported events; count others separately
method.positive_decision_rule: source outcome signal deserves native opt-in follow-up only when on original-supported observations, original Brier is at least 0.02 lower than uninformative p=.5 and on matched-permutation support original Brier is at least 0.02 lower than permuted labels, with at least 100 matched events pooled over native roles; otherwise do not implement/promote based on the mechanism
method.measured: Brier, support, matched support, source change rate, selected action diversity, alternative permuted/inverted Brier, original goal rewards only as factual side metadata
method.result_interpretation: even positive Brier only shows *on-policy predictive association*, not benefit of selecting another action, causal generalization or goal success
